function: DRL (double-agent conditional SAC) designs MF-RIS modes, amplitudes and phases plus transceiver beamformers to minimize long-term AirComp aggregation MSE under imperfect CSI (p. 1, 3, 7).
system: Uplink AirComp: 4-antenna BS, 2 robots with 2 antennas each, MF-RIS (simultaneous reflection, refraction, amplification) with 36 elements, 3.5 GHz (p. 3, 10, 11).
method: Reinforcement learning: double-agent soft actor-critic (CSAC); agent d picks discrete RIS modes, agent c continuous transceiver and RIS beamforming; asynchronous updates; 10^6 training steps (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician RIS links, Rayleigh direct link, distance-based path loss, Gaussian CSI error and channel aging; no standard model or dataset (p. 4-5, 11).
test_conditions: Same simulated environment for training and evaluation; average MSE over training steps; sweeps of CSI error mu, correlation rho, RIS power, N, K (p. 11-13).
baselines: Learned: single SAC, random-mode SAC, DDPG-DDPG, DQN-SAC; active-RIS and no-RIS cases with SAC; non-learned: alternating optimization (AO) of [47] (p. 10-13).
metrics: Long-term average aggregation MSE, episodic reward, MF-RIS power consumption, reflected and refracted amplitudes (p. 11-14).
complexity: Big-O training and inference complexity formulas, Table III compares schemes; inference 0.04 s on RTX 4060 GPU vs about 27 s for AO per frame (p. 10-12).
q1_support: p. 4: "we consider a Rician fading model for the MF-RIS-aided channels, while a Rayleigh fading model for the direct channel"; custom simulator with path loss from Table II (p. 11), and no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "The average MSE in training step t is given by"; MSE is measured in the same simulated setup during training, with sweeps over mu, rho, power, N and K as separate settings, and no test on an unseen scenario or after adaptation.
q3_support: p. 10: "DDPG-DDPG: This case replaces SAC algorithm with DDPG [46]" and "AO: A traditional optimization method based on AO in [47] is adopted"; the MSE of CSAC is compared with both (Figs. 6-9, p. 11-13).
q4_support: p. 10: "the problem-solving computational complexity of the proposed CSAC is" O(2 O1) in Eq. (31); Table III (p. 11) compares schemes and p. 12 gives 0.04 s inference on an RTX 4060 GPU.
q5_support: p. 10: "The three-dimensional (3D) simulation setup of the considered IoRT system is illustrated in Fig. 4"; all data come from this self-built simulator, and the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 3 and not 7: the learned part configures the MF-RIS and the beamformers, and the aggregated data are robot sensing data in AirComp with no federated learning, so area 7 (model aggregation) does not fit; the reviewer may reconsider. q3 is 1 because DDPG-DDPG and DQN-SAC apply standard DRL algorithms (DDPG, DQN) to the same problem inside the double-agent scaffold, while single SAC and random-SAC are ablations and were not counted; AO [47] is the non-learned baseline, compared on MSE (Fig. 7). Tables I-III were read from the page images (p. 2, 11).
